exercises.title: Array Mapping Basics
exercises.description: Practice transforming arrays using the map method.
exercises.context: Array mapping is extremely common in frontend development when rendering lists, transforming API responses, or formatting data before displaying it in the UI.
technicalNotes: map creates a new array without mutating the original array.
The callback runs once for every element.
Arrow functions are commonly used with map.

exercises.title: Filter Active Users
exercises.description: Filter objects inside an array based on a condition.
exercises.context: Filtering collections is used constantly in dashboards, admin panels, search systems, and data processing pipelines.
technicalNotes: filter returns a new array containing only matching items.
The original array remains unchanged.
Boolean expressions determine whether an item is included.

exercises.title: Basic Fetch Request
exercises.description: Practice making a simple asynchronous request using fetch.
exercises.context: Fetching data from APIs is one of the most common tasks in web development.
technicalNotes: fetch returns a Promise.
await pauses execution until the Promise resolves.
response.json converts the response body into JavaScript data.

exercises.title: Object Destructuring Practice
exercises.description: Extract values from objects using destructuring syntax.
exercises.context: Destructuring is heavily used in React props, API responses, and configuration objects.
technicalNotes: Destructuring simplifies object property access.
Template literals improve string readability.
Destructuring is very common in modern JavaScript frameworks.

exercises.title: Basic Debounce Function
exercises.description: Create a debounce utility to delay function execution.
exercises.context: Debounce is commonly used in search bars, resize listeners, and auto-save systems to improve performance.
technicalNotes: Closures allow access to variables outside the returned function.
clearTimeout prevents multiple executions.
Debouncing improves performance by reducing repeated calls.

exercises.title: Calculate Cart Total
exercises.description: Use reduce to calculate the total price of items in a shopping cart.
exercises.context: reduce is commonly used in ecommerce applications, analytics dashboards, and financial summaries where values need to be accumulated.
technicalNotes: reduce accumulates values into a single result.
The accumulator stores the current total.
Initial values prevent unexpected behavior.

exercises.title: Loop Through Notifications
exercises.description: Practice iterating through arrays using a for...of loop.
exercises.context: Loops are used everywhere in programming to process collections, notifications, messages, and API data.
technicalNotes: for...of simplifies array iteration.
It is cleaner than traditional index-based loops for simple traversal.
Each iteration exposes the current item directly.

exercises.title: Generate URL Slug
exercises.description: Convert a title into a URL-friendly slug.
exercises.context: Slug generation is heavily used in blogs, CMS systems, ecommerce platforms, and SEO-friendly URLs.
technicalNotes: trim removes extra spaces.
replace with regex helps normalize strings.
Lowercase URLs improve consistency.

exercises.title: Save Theme Preference
exercises.description: Store and retrieve user preferences using localStorage.
exercises.context: Persisting user settings like themes and preferences is common in modern frontend applications.
technicalNotes: localStorage persists data between browser sessions.
Stored values are always strings.
Fallback values improve robustness.

exercises.title: Sort Products by Price
exercises.description: Sort objects inside an array based on numeric values.
exercises.context: Sorting collections is fundamental in ecommerce stores, dashboards, ranking systems, and admin panels.
technicalNotes: sort mutates the original array.
Compare callbacks define sorting behavior.
Numeric sorting requires subtraction logic.
